script.base: SF is a 2.5-point favorite in a 47.5 outdoor game (implied SF 25.0, NYG 22.5), so the book expects a close, moderate-scoring game with no blowout flag and starters finishing. Base flow stays run-leaning on both sides: SF feeds Christian McCaffrey (49 carries, 208 rush yards and 22 targets, 172 rec yards in weeks 6-8) into a NYG run defense allowing 6.06 YPC, while NYG uses Cam Skattebo (38 carries, 170 yards) and Jaxson Dart's legs (20 carries, 89 yards) and still gets Wan'Dale Robinson about 7.7 targets a game inside a ~25-target NYG pass volume.
script.flip1: SF jumps ahead by two scores because NYG is without CBs Paulson Adebo, Cordale Flott and Art Green. NYG then abandons the run, Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy carries die, and Wan'Dale Robinson plus Theo Johnson targets spike, while SF clocks it and Jauan Jennings/Kendrick Bourne deep yards stall.
script.flip2: Brock Purdy (toe, questionable) sits or is limited and center Jake Brendel (out) plus unsaved outdoor weather turn it into a low-efficiency slog. Deep air yards do not convert, and NYG — already with tackle Jermaine Eluemunor doubtful — cannot run on SF's 4.16 YPC defense, so both the pass overs and the rushing overs fail together.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report only; inactives ~90 minutes before kick are not in the pack. NYG: Eluemunor Doubtful (pectoral) is the OT loss — rush efficiency down, more quick throws, which helps Wan'Dale Robinson and Theo Johnson and hurts Skattebo's efficiency and deep shots to Lil'Jordan Humphrey (146 air yards) and Jalin Hyatt. Daniel Bellinger Doubtful (neck) had only 5 targets but 109 yards and 101 air in weeks 6-8; Johnson (15 targets, 113 yards) is the next TE, a small volume bump not a role takeover. Adebo Out, Flott Out, Art Green Out, Rico Payton Questionable and Jevon Holland Questionable strip the secondary and funnel SF throws, but that is the other sideline. Chauncey Golston Out (neck) slightly eases SF's protection. SF: Ricky Pearsall Out (knee) leaves the recent target pile with McCaffrey (22), Jennings (17), Bourne (15), Jake Tonges (8) and George Kittle (7). Brendel Out (hamstring) with Ben Bartch and Spencer Burford Questionable is an OL hit: pressure up, rush efficiency down, quick throws up, deep WR yards down — this is why McCaffrey rush over is not a leg. Purdy Questionable (toe) can flip the whole SF script; M.Jones already has 10 carries and 49 rush yards in the L3 sample, so a backup-QB game may already be partly in the recent numbers. Bryce Huff Out and Yetur Gross-Matos Out, with Jordan Elliott and Sam Okuayinonu Questionable, thin SF's pass rush; Dee Winters Questionable (knee) is the LB soft spot for NYG TEs and slots.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, man/zone rate or MOFO/MOFC split is in the pack. Proxy only: SF allows 11.52 YPA on middle throws (50 attempts) versus 6.22 left (112) and 5.91 right (105), so the middle is the bleed. NYG allows 7.8 middle (50), 6.66 left (109) and 6.59 right (135), and is much worse against the run than the pass.
matchup.pressure: NYG blitz rate 32%; SF EPA/dropback is 0.11 when blitzed versus 0.08 when not, so SF is not blitz-fragile. SF blitz rate 25%; NYG EPA/dropback is -0.07 when blitzed versus 0.02 when not. That NYG blitz weakness is partly offset because SF is without Huff and Gross-Matos, so season pressure rates overstate what Dart will see.
matchup.bleeds: NYG bleeds the run (6.06 YPC, 37 runs of 10+ in 8 games) and is down three cornerbacks. SF's run defense is the strength (4.16 YPC, only 16 runs of 10+) and the pass bleed is specifically the middle (11.52 YPA), not the outside (right 5.91, left 6.22). SF has allowed 22 passes of 20+ for 276 yards; NYG has allowed 21 for 313.
matchup.overlap: NYG's top option is Wan'Dale Robinson (23 targets, 227 yards, 232 air yards in weeks 6-8, about 31% of the 74 charted NYG targets) and that usage sits in the short/intermediate and slot area where SF's middle YPA is the defensive hole. Theo Johnson (15 targets, 113 yards, 107 air) is the TE overlap on the same middle, with Winters questionable. The other overlap — Jennings (222 air yards, only 83 rec yards) and Bourne (221 air, 200 yards) versus a gutted NYG secondary — is real but fights SF's own OL injuries, so it is not a leg.

McCaffrey rush 57, 54, 129, 25 and rec 82, 57, 72, 43: the 129 is a boom and the latest game is a 25-yard floor. Jennings 24, 7, 31, 45 is trending up but still only 83 yards on 222 air in the L3. Bourne 142, 142, 14, 44 is two explosion games plus a 14-yard miss — treat the 142s as fluky until play-by-play exists. Tonges 58, 41, 58, 2 vanished last game. Wan'Dale 30, 84, 95, 48: WR1 role, L3 average 75.7, latest game cooled to 48. Johnson 33, 27, 66, 20: three of four over 23.5, latest 20. Skattebo rush 59, 98, 60, 12 and Tracy 29, 6, 46, 39 show a committee plus Dart's 20 carries, and Skattebo just had a 12-yard game against the kind of front SF actually is. Malik Nabers last4 71, 167, 13, 20 across only 4 season games and he has zero targets in weeks 6-8, so he is not in the current offense. Brian Robinson 21, 12, 0, 36 is a change-of-pace, not the engine.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. SF, even without a charted shell, parked a linebacker in the hook and held Wan'Dale to another 30-48 yard afternoon while Dart (20 rushes in the L3) and Skattebo (38 carries) kept NYG on the ground in a one-score game that never forced 8 targets. Eluemunor was only doubtful and played, so the quick-throw bump never came, and unsaved November wind killed the 10-air-yards-per-target routes. Johnson lost because Bellinger played, the 66-yard game was one explosive the way Bellinger's 109 on 5 targets already warned, and the week-8 line of 20 was the real role against a defense that just held the run to 4.16 YPC and let NYG stay on the ground. That counter is real — especially for Johnson, which is why he is a lean — but it is not stronger than the read: both rates were already produced in a run-heavy NYG sample and still cleared these lines on average. The Wan'Dale leg stays, flagged, not cut.
slip_story: One story only: a competitive NYG pass-to-the-middle game, not a shootout and not an SF blowout. Wan'Dale over and Johnson over win together if Dart takes his recent ~25 dropbacks and SF's middle (11.52 YPA) stays the weak spot. Do not add Skattebo or Tracy rush overs (those need NYG to lean run into a 4.16 YPC defense and a doubtful tackle), do not add a game-total under (it fights the same pass production), and do not add Jennings or Bourne overs (those need a healthy Purdy and a functional SF line against the other secondary). McCaffrey rush over is the other-story candidate and is off this slip because Brendel out conflicts with it.
